target.title: feat(computer-use): control macOS nodes via screenshots and input injection
target.body:
Related: #97333
Related: #97938
Related: #69799
Related: #44759

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw could screenshot a paired macOS node but could not act on it: there was no way for an agent to move the pointer, click, type, scroll, or press keys on a node. Computer-use ("drive the desktop from a screenshot loop") was a repeatedly requested capability (#97333) with no end-to-end path — no input-injection node command, no agent tool, and no permission/arming model to make it safe.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the first end-to-end computer-use path, scoped to macOS nodes, as a bundled `computer-use` plugin plus a native node executor.

- **Node protocol** (`openclaw.node.computer.v1`): a low-risk `computer.status` read (display geometry, cursor, permission state) and a dangerous `computer.input` write (one action: move / click / mouse down·up / drag / scroll / key / type / hold). Screenshots reuse the existing `screen.snapshot`.
- **macOS executor**: the Mac app node handles `computer.*` natively via CoreGraphics event injection, gated behind a new "Allow Computer Control" setting (default off) and Accessibility trust. Pointer coordinates are interpreted in reference-screenshot pixels and mapped back to global screen points, so the model can click where it sees.
- **Plugin**: registers the `computer` agent tool (drives the screenshot→act loop, one action per call, returning a fresh screenshot to the model), and two node-invoke policies. `computer.input` is `dangerous` — it requires operator opt-in via `gateway.nodes.allowCommands` plus per-session approval, with `allow-always` arming the node for a bounded window (`computer arm/disarm/status`).
- **Safety**: screenshots go to the model, not auto-delivered to chat channels (avoids the on-screen-secret leak class in #44759); the executor lives in the app that holds the TCC grants, not an ambient CLI binary (the concern in #69799); screen content is treated as untrusted input (prompt-injection posture documented in the skill and tool description).

Non-goals (follow-ups): provider-native Anthropic `computer_20251124` tool-type transport, Linux/Windows/sandbox-desktop executors, and time-bounded persistent arming beyond the in-window model.

## User Impact

On a paired macOS node with the plugin enabled, "Allow Computer Control" turned on, and `computer.input` opted into `gateway.nodes.allowCommands`, an agent can look at the screen and operate the Mac — click buttons, type into fields, use keyboard shortcuts, scroll, and drag — with an explicit approval/arming gate. It is macOS-only for now and off by default at every layer.

## Evidence

- **Swift (validated locally):** `apps/shared/OpenClawKit` builds clean; the OpenClaw app target compiles (`swift build --target OpenClaw`, 1070/1070). Swift tests pass: `swift test` → 44 tests across `ComputerInputGeometryTests` (coordinate mapping + Codable, 7/7), `ComputerKeyMapTests` (key-name/chord mapping), and `MacNodeModeCoordinatorTests`/`MacNodeRuntimeTests` (caps/command advertisement + dispatch). `swiftformat --lint` clean.
- **TypeScript:** `pnpm test extensions/computer-use` → 29 passed (4 files). Covers the arming gate (`input-policy.test.ts`: not-armed → approval; deny/null → not invoked; allow-once → invoke without arming; allow-always → armed with expiry; already-armed → invoked without approval; non-macOS → rejected), the tool schema + convenience-click translation, arm-state expiry, and plugin registration (two policies + tool + command + keyed store). Package-manifest contract test → 40 passed. `oxfmt --check` clean. Plugin inventory regenerated (`pnpm plugins:inventory:gen`).
- **Live input injection** (CGEvent + Accessibility TCC) requires a real Mac with the app built and Accessibility granted; it is **not** exercised by CI. This is the remaining manual verification gate before land.

Stacked on the Computer Use manifest contract PR (base). Do not land before live-injection verification on a real Mac.
